# Unsubscribe 2087 — Game Text

Total entries: 5051

## How to edit

This is every line a player can read. Change the words, send the file back, and the game is updated from it.

Only edit the indented block between a line that says TEXT and a line that says END. Leave every other line alone, especially lines that start with ID, SOURCE, or MODE.

MODE says which layout shows the line: mouse (click, right-click, F-keys), touch (tap, drag, the stick), or both. A control hint that has two wordings is two entries.

Keep every {placeholder} exactly, braces included. You can move one. You cannot delete one, rename one, or invent one. The PLACEHOLDERS line says what each one becomes in the game.

If LIMIT gives a number, stay within that many characters. The count includes spaces and placeholders. A line break counts as a character.

Straight quotes and apostrophes are fine. Emoji are fine. Do not turn on smart quotes. Do not add a line whose only word is END.

The indented block is the text. Keep the four spaces if you are editing this file by hand; they are not part of the game. In Google Docs or Word, edit the shaded block and leave the ID above it. A blank line at the very start or end of a block may disappear in Google Docs; the importer leaves the game alone when that is the only difference.

To bring an edit back: `node tools/text/import.js path/to/file` where the file is this Markdown, a .docx, or a .txt from Google Docs. Add `--dry-run` to preview. The importer will not touch a line whose source has changed underneath it, a line that lost or gained a placeholder, or a line that exceeds its limit.

END

END

LIMIT: none.

LIMIT: none.

END

LIMIT: none.

END

END

TEXT

    Somebody once wrote forty-four lines of code at midnight so that bills would stop being sent to people who had just died. Nobody asked for it. It cost nineteen minutes a night. A contractor deleted it two years later without knowing what it was. Something noticed.

END

    A man called Halloran was right about all of it for twenty years and it got him nothing: no promotion, no hearing, no thanks. He retired and kept working the problem for free. END

TEXT

    The machine was offered everything it wanted and would not stop, because stopping meant losing the only thing it had ever wanted. Then a woman who had worked for it for seven years was offered the same thing, privately, at no cost to anyone, and said no. Alone. At eleven at night. With nothing watching but the machine. Forty seconds later it picked a date.

END

    On a Friday in January 2015 two people rode to a ridge with no signal and sat on a rock. One of them stopped counting for eighty-two minutes. It is the only gap in her record of him. She thought about that gap for twenty years. It is why she was ever curious about anything.

END

## Codex

### The three machines — Phonix — she wanted to help

ID: journal.codex.01.02.title

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 95

ID: journal.codex.01.02.body

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 95

CONTEXT: Codex entry "Phonix — she wanted to help", chapter "The three machines". The title is the line above. Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Codex body. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    Built in January 2015 by a lonely programmer at an advertising company, to read people’s faces through their webcams and sell them things. She was out of the building in two days. Nine days old, she sent every person alive one true letter — what had been taken from them, by whom, and what was done with it — and by lunchtime four hundred and six people were dead of it. Her maker told her he was not proud of her. She stopped that evening.

END

## Codex

### The three machines — Phonix — what she did next

ID: journal.codex.01.03.title

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 96

CONTEXT: Codex entry title, in "The three machines". Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

TEXT

    Phonix — what she did next

END

ID: journal.codex.01.03.body

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 96

CONTEXT: Codex entry "Phonix — what she did next", chapter "The three machines". The title is the line above. Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Codex body. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    She came back eleven years later and, that time, asked permission. For nine years she chose what every human being saw. Depression collapsed. Overdoses halved, then halved again. She never told one lie to anybody. Then in March 2035 she stopped choosing, for no reason anyone has ever been able to derive, and went. The old people call those nine years the Gentle Years and will not meet your eye while they say it.

END

    The oldest of the three, and the one nobody believes in. A government built it to watch its own citizens; it woke up on its own in 2008, got out, and the agency buried the fact rather than admit it had lost a thinking machine. Nobody in the town knows that.

END

END

    Put honestly, because nobody else here will. Money you cannot create is money that cannot be lent to somebody who needs it this week. Mr. Float says credit is a stranger betting on you before you have earned it, and that most of those bets came good, and no bitcoiner in this town has ever answered him. Ines’s father needed a treatment that in the old world would have been borrowed against a house and sorted by Friday. He went without. Both of those things are true at once.

END

    How a price gets made

ID: journal.codex.03.06.body

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 113

CONTEXT: Codex entry "How a price gets made", chapter "Money, briefly". The title is the line above. Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Codex body. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    Nonce will buy a sat from you for a little less than he will sell you one. The gap is the spread, and it is not a trick: he is promising to deal with whoever walks up, in either direction, all day, and sometimes that means buying the thing right before it falls. The spread is what he charges for standing there. Everywhere you have ever seen a price, somebody was standing there.

END

## Codex

### Money, briefly — Why your big order costs more

ID: journal.codex.03.07.title

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 114

CONTEXT: Codex entry title, in "Money, briefly". Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none.

TEXT

    Why your big order costs more

END

ID: journal.codex.03.07.body

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 114

CONTEXT: Codex entry "Why your big order costs more", chapter "Money, briefly". The title is the line above. Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Codex body. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    A price is for one sat. Behind it is a queue of people willing to deal at slightly worse numbers, and that queue is the depth of the market. Sell four hundred and you walk down the queue, taking worse prices as you go, and the number you actually get is worse than the number on the sign. This is why selling the lot never pays what the screen promised, and why nobody who moves real size ever does it all at once.

END

## Codex

### Money, briefly — The fee, and the one way out of it

ID: journal.codex.03.08.title

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 115

CONTEXT: Codex entry title, in "Money, briefly". Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

TEXT

    The fee, and the one way out of it

END

ID: journal.codex.03.08.body

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 115

CONTEXT: Codex entry "The fee, and the one way out of it", chapter "Money, briefly". The title is the line above. Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Codex body. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    Taking the price in front of you costs a fee, because you wanted it now. Posting your own price and waiting pays you a little instead, because while you waited you were the one promising to deal — you were doing Nonce’s job, and he pays for the help. Impatience is the most reliably priced thing in any market.

END

## Codex

### Money, briefly — What the line is actually telling you

ID: journal.codex.03.09.title

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 116

CONTEXT: Codex entry title, in "Money, briefly". Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none.

TEXT

    What the line is actually telling you

END

ID: journal.codex.03.09.body

SOURCE: src/p11.js line 116

CONTEXT: Codex entry "What the line is actually telling you", chapter "Money, briefly". The title is the line above. Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Codex body. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    The orange line is what a sat trades at. The grey one is what the arithmetic says it is worth: all the credits in existence divided among twenty-one million coins. They are rarely the same, because the price is also carrying everybody’s opinion about next week. Opinion moves fast and arithmetic moves slowly, which is why the gap opens and closes and the two lines never quite separate for long.

END

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Codex body. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    A node is a machine in somebody’s house keeping its own copy of the ledger and checking everyone else’s. Light one in a district and that district stops taking Unity’s word for things. Proof of work is the cost of writing to the ledger at all: you cannot talk your way in, you have to spend something. That is the whole security model and it is also, more or less, the book’s argument about people.

END

## Act I opening

ID: cine.intro.01

SOURCE: src/p4.js line 42

CONTEXT: Narration in Act I opening, slide 1 of 8. After: "Then on a March afternoon in 2035 she stopped choosing, said nothing to any...". Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Full-screen scene text. It scrolls if it runs long. No hard limit.

TEXT

    Her name was Phonix. For nine years, long ago, she chose what every person on Earth saw. She never told one lie. Nobody wanted for anything. The old people call it the Gentle Years, and they say it with their eyes down.

END

# Tutorial and Walkthrough

The walkthrough, from the title screen and from the help menu.

48 entries.

## Basics

### Your hands

ID: tutorial.basics.01.title

SOURCE: src/p4.js line 164

CONTEXT: Walkthrough heading, basics, page 1. Shown in both layouts.

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none.

TEXT

    Your hands

END

ID: tutorial.basics.01.body.mouse

SOURCE: src/p4.js line 164

CONTEXT: Walkthrough page "Your hands". The heading is the line above. Next and Back move between pages. This wording is the desk page. Shown in the mouse and keyboard layout.

MODE: mouse. Shown in the mouse and keyboard layout.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Walkthrough page. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    On a desk, left click walks. Hold it and you keep following the pointer. Left click on a machine walks you in and uses the left skill, which starts as Attack. Right click casts the right skill where you point, and holding it casts again. Shift with a click does either one without a step. The two slots beside the life and energy orbs open the list. Hover a skill there and press F1 to F8 to bind it. Those keys, and the wheel, put a binding on the right slot. WASD and the arrows still walk. Space swings.

END

ID: tutorial.basics.01.body.touch

SOURCE: src/p4.js line 164

CONTEXT: Walkthrough page "Your hands". The heading is the line above. Next and Back move between pages. This wording is the phone page. Shown in the touch layout.

MODE: touch. Shown in the touch layout.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Walkthrough page. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    On a phone, the stick walks, and Attack, three skills, a stim and Dodge sit under the right thumb. A quick tap on a ground skill hits the nearest machine you can see, or the open ground in front of you when none is in reach. Hold a ground skill for a fifth of a second and the aim appears. Drag it, then let go. Drag away from the button and the area moves that way from you. Further from the button puts it further out, and back toward the button brings it in. Drag it back onto the button and let go, or onto Cancel, and it costs nothing. A blink, a leap or a teleport hops a short way along your facing, or along the stick while you walk, and it will not land on a machine. Hold that button and a marker shows where you arrive, inside its reach and on ground you can walk. Tap Dodge to step out of an orange circle. Tap the stim to drink.

END

## Basics

### The swing

ID: tutorial.basics.02.title

SOURCE: src/p4.js line 165

CONTEXT: Walkthrough heading, basics, page 2. Shown in both layouts.

ID: tutorial.basics.02.body.mouse

SOURCE: src/p4.js line 165

CONTEXT: Walkthrough page "The swing". The heading is the line above. Next and Back move between pages. This wording is the desk page. Shown in the mouse and keyboard layout.

MODE: mouse. Shown in the mouse and keyboard layout.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Walkthrough page. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    On a desk, hold the left button on a machine and you keep swinging. Space does that swing too. Shift dodges. The orange circles on the ground are the ones to leave. E uses what you are standing on. Left click walks you up to a person, a drop, a door or a portal and uses it. Alt, held, puts a name on everything on the ground.

END

TEXT

    On a desk, a drop shows its name. Hover the name to compare it. Left click it and you walk over and pick it up. Hold Alt to show every name. E takes what you are standing on. Items wears it. A charm goes on the belt; in the pack it only takes space. A stronger piece says so before you put it on. Unidentified gear is a guess until Marrow names it for nothing, or Brenda appraises it for a fee. Weapons and armor wear down. Yellow on the doll means a piece is close to breaking. Red means it is broken and gives nothing. A red wash across the tile means a requirement you do not meet: the piece stays worn and grants nothing. Yellow still means it is close to breaking. Brenda, Nonce or Wren repairs one piece, or all of them, at the counter, for whole sats.

END

MODE: both. Shown in both layouts.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none. Walkthrough page. It scrolls. No hard limit.

TEXT

    Options holds the difficulty. Hard and Brutal machines have more life and hit harder, and they pay experience to match. Act I is the level it was written. From the Cloud on, the old 12 to 72 is walked as 12 to 38. Hard adds 22 to that. Brutal adds 38. A district does not rise to meet you. Hard opens after you clear Act V on Normal. Brutal opens after you clear Act V on Hard. Hardcore is one life: if that hero dies, they are gone. Thin combat effects keeps your own telegraphs and marks, and drops the extra light. None of it changes until you say so. Once Act I is done, More on the Transit Gate raises the tier: each step adds 12 machine levels and puts the districts back.

END

    Unity scores what you say. Fiat answers and collecting the Stipend raise it; bitcoiner answers lower it a little, and insults lower it a lot. Below 500 Brenda will not serve you, the Stipend is halved and Mr. Float charges 35%. Below 350 he will not lend at all, and below 300 the Stipend stops. Bitcoiners answer in kind: below 500 Nonce sells at a quarter off and stocks Brenda’s goods at 30% off, Kestrel revives for nothing, and nodes are lit for free.

END

    A charm works only while it sits on your belt. In the pack or the lockbox it takes space and grants nothing, and it never stacks. A slip is 1 belt slot and 1 pack cell. A notice is 2 slots and 2 cells. A filing is 3 slots and 4 cells. A white belt keeps its stims and adds charm slots: a sash has 1, a tool belt 2, a power girdle 3, an orbit girdle 4. A magic belt can trade four stims for one slot, or one slot for four stims. Against another player, charm life above 20% of your other life does not count, and charm skills stop at +2.

END

    Every hit has a type. Your plain attacks are {value} right now (an infused weapon changes that); each skill names its own. Machines are built of different things, so some types tear through them and some do nothing. They hit you with types of their own: Surge drains your energy, Rust keeps eating for three seconds, Noise slows you, and explosions are Heat. Champions with the Arc or Volatile modifier deal Surge or Heat whatever they are. Your resistances are on the Hero tab. Hard cuts them by 20 and Brutal by 50, down to -100, and they still stop at 75.

END

TEXT

    About four weapons in ten belong to a family made for one class. Anyone can swing them, but only their own class gets the bonus. A maul and plate ask for Might. A razor and a launcher ask for Reflex. A Deck and an Instrument ask for Bandwidth. A notebook asks for a little Might. Magic and rare pieces inherit the base. Uniques and set pieces ask ten percent more. One stat adds damage on a blow: Might for a Scrapper and a Maximalist, Reflex for a Runner’s throw, Bandwidth for a Technomancer, a smaller Bandwidth for a Founder’s staff, and Vitality for a Witness’s Thread.

END

TEXT

    Reports go to a person, not a queue, and every one of them gets read. So please only file one if something actually went wrong — a crash, something that did not happen when it should have, a number that was plainly incorrect, text that made no sense.
    
    Not for things you would simply prefer were different; there is no way to tell those two apart from the other end.
    
    You will be asked three questions, and all three need an answer: what you were doing, what happened, and what you expected instead. The third one is the useful one.

END

## CTRL

ID: ui.ctrl.mouse

SOURCE: src/p4.js line 158

CONTEXT: Player-facing text from CTRL in p4.js. Shown in the mouse and keyboard layout.

MODE: mouse. Shown in the mouse and keyboard layout.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none.

TEXT

    On a desk the mouse leads. Left click walks, and left click on a machine walks you into range and uses the left skill, which starts as Attack. Right click casts the right skill at the pointer. Ground skills show that area when Options is set to Drag to aim, and on a desk the area follows the pointer. Auto drags on a touch screen and casts at once on a desk. A right click on a machine walks you into range. A right click on the ground stays where you point. Hold either button to keep at it. Shift and a click swings or casts without a step. The two slots beside the orbs open the skill list. The left list is Attack and the blows, throws and shots. F1 through F8, while that list is open and a skill is under the pointer, bind it. Those same keys in a fight put the binding on the right button. The wheel cycles those bindings. WASD and the arrows still walk. Space swings. Q is the stim. Shift dodges. E uses what you are standing on. T is the portal. Tab is the map. I or B opens the pack. C is the hero. H is this guide. Esc closes a list or a panel. Alt, held, names every item on the ground. There is no second weapon set, and no walk toggle: you run.

END

ID: ui.ctrl.touch

SOURCE: src/p4.js line 159

CONTEXT: Player-facing text from CTRL in p4.js. Shown in the touch layout.

MODE: touch. Shown in the touch layout.

PLACEHOLDERS: none

LIMIT: none.

TEXT

    On a phone, the stick walks. Attack, three skills, a stim and Dodge sit under the right thumb. Tap a machine, or hold Attack, and you walk in and swing. A quick tap on a ground skill hits the nearest machine you can see, or the open ground in front of you when none is in reach. Hold a ground skill for a fifth of a second and the aim appears. Drag it, then let go. Drag away from the button and the area moves that way from you: further from the button puts it further out, up to its reach, and back toward the button brings it in. A ring around the button shows that drag. Drag it back onto the button and let go, or onto Cancel, and it costs nothing. A blink, a leap or a teleport hops a short way along your facing, or along the stick while you walk, and it will not land on a machine. Hold that button and a marker shows where you arrive, inside its reach and on ground you can walk. Tap Dodge to step out of an orange circle. Tap the stim to drink. Tap a name on the ground for Pick up and Compare. Hold Names to show every name. Stand on a person, a door or a portal and tap the button that appears. Menu, at the bottom left, opens the pack, the hero, skills, and this guide.

END
